patch.value: The publish-attestation scan judged shell text with a regular expression, so real unattested publishes scanned clean

The guard decided whether any publish omits provenance by blanking quoted spans and splitting the remainder on three operators. Blanking deletes the very argument under audit, so a publish carrying an attestation reads as one without it, and the reverse is worse: an eval or a bash dash-c wrapping a publish disappears from the scan entirely, leaving an attested sibling elsewhere in the file to carry the audit to green. The operator split also misses a backgrounding ampersand, a pipe written without surrounding spaces, and command substitution. Replaced by a real tokeniser that resolves what each command actually runs.

value.author: claude
value.text: Extracted scripts/shell-command-scan.ts: a tokeniser that tracks single, double and backslash quoting per character while keeping the quoted text in the token, splits on the full operator set (semicolon, ampersand, double-ampersand, pipe, double-pipe, newline) regardless of surrounding whitespace, and unwraps interpreter shells so that eval and bash dash-c bodies are re-scanned as commands rather than swallowed as string arguments. The attestation guard now asks the tokeniser for command name and arguments instead of pattern-matching text. Covered to 100/100/100/100; test/coverage-gate.test.ts stub updated to enumerate the new source file, which the gate requires.

author: claude
message: That test file does not exist; the tokeniser is exercised from the attestation guard's suite

value.author: claude
value.text: Adversarially measured, not reasoned about. Fourteen bypass shapes drawn from the Greptile findings raised across the fleet were run against the tokeniser: global options before the subcommand, a quoted subcommand, a quoted flag, eval, bash -c, a combined short-option cluster (bash -ec), sh -c, a pipe without surrounding spaces, a single backgrounding ampersand, command substitution, backticks, an env prefix, a subshell, and a package runner. Thirteen were already caught; npx was not, so package runners and their own option words are now consumed as wrappers. A second round found the two-word runners (pnpm dlx, yarn exec, bun x) still escaping, and those are consumed only when the second word completes the pair, so an unrelated pnpm install is not re-pointed at its first argument. Both new rules were revert-checked: removing either drops the suite from 40 passing to a failure.

value.note: npx and its own option words are consumed as a wrapper

PM_PATH=/tmp/pm-ops-jhc8 PM_GLOBAL_PATH=/tmp/pm-ops-jhc8-g node --test --test-name-pattern "a runner spelled as two words" test/verify-release-publish-attestation.test.ts

value.author: claude
value.text: Propagating the guard to the fleet exposed that it was not self-contained: it imported six shared symbols from the changelog-date gate, a file only four of the sixteen packages have. The dependency also pointed the wrong way, an attestation gate reaching into a changelog gate for shell-text helpers. The shell-text helpers and the two shared gate shapes now live in shell-command-scan.ts, and isMainInvocation moved to scripts/main-invocation.ts, which is the factoring pm-beads had already arrived at independently and whose realpath comparison also recognises a symlinked entry point. Both gates now depend on the shared modules rather than on each other.
